atoms.b:
A fuse is a ((safety)) device found in things that use or transport electricity. It stops too much ((current)) flowing through and protects us from ((fires)) and electrocution.

When the current becomes too ((high)), the thin wire inside the fuse will ((break)), leaving a gap in the circuit. This stops the flow of electricity and prevents the device from breaking or ((setting)) on fire.

instruction.text: Select the switch that is different to the rest.

feedback.end: This is a picture of a fuse box, which can be found in most buildings. Each switch monitors a different section of the building’s electricity supply and turns itself off if the circuit becomes overloaded.

instruction.text: The buzzer in this circuit won’t make any noise. Can you see any issues with this circuit?

feedback.end: Since fuses can be found inside of components, we can’t see the problem just by looking at the circuit. Let’s see if that’s why the buzzer won’t work.

instruction.text: Is there a problem with the buzzer’s fuse?

feedback.end: The buzzer’s fuse has blown. This means that electricity can no longer flow through it and the circuit is open.

Fuses are there to protect us from potentially dangerous electrical circuits, so replacing it with a wire would not be a good idea. The best choice would be to replace it with a new fuse of the same type.

atoms.a: What should be done to make the buzzer work again?
b: Remove the fuse and put a wire in instead.
Replace every part of the circuit.
++Replace the fuse with a new, working one.
